entries.title: Proverbs 24:1
segments:
Envious against evil men--desire to be with them; because of their present success. 
 
Since the prosperity of the ungodly leads only to ruin, no wise man will envy them, or wish to cast in his lot with them.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:4
segments: Success comes not by chance, but by prudent counsels and actions.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:6
segments: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war; that is, with success; an illustration of the declaration in the preceding verse, that wisdom and knowledge give strength.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:7
segments: In the gate; where causes are tried and deliberations held on weighty matters.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:9
segments: The thought of foolishness; the plans and pursuits of foolish men. fill out the two clauses thus: The thoughts and actions of fools and scorners are sinful, and therefore an abomination to men.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:10
segments: God sends upon men adversity for the purpose of exercising their faith and fortitude, and thus increasing these graces; but hed who faints under the discipline loses the benefit of it, and becomes weaker instead of stronger.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:11
segments: Drawn unto death--ready to be slain; unjustly seized and dragged to a violent death.  This precept applies primarily to magistrates, and also to private persons according to their ability to help the oppressed and unjustly condemned.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:12
segments: It is the duty of all men, as they have opportunity, to succor and relieve the oppressed.  And since the worst bondage is that of sin and ignorance, no man may on any ground excuse himself from doing what lies in his power for the rescue of the millions who are held under its thraldom.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:13
segments:
vv 13-14. 
 
  Eat thou honey-- so shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul; that is, I commend thee for eating honey, because it is good; much more, then, do thou gain the knowledge of wisdom, which is better than honey.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:14
segments: No possession yields so precious a revenue as wisdom.  It makes men rich for time and eternity.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:16
segments:
The wicked shall fall into mischief; out of which he shall never rise again. 
 
The just man falls for his discipline, and God will raise him up again; but the wicked falls for his destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:17
segments: Joy at the calamity of an enemy is a heinous sin, and one which God will visit with condign punishment.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:21
segments:
Them that are given to change; seditious men, like Absalom, who seek to change the established order of government. 
 
They who follow discontented innovators, do it to their destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:22
segments: The ruin of them both; the ruin which will come upon such men from both God and the king, whose wrath they have incurred.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:23
segments:
These things also; the maxims that follow to the end of the chapter. 
 
  Belong to the wise; either, should be observed by the wise, or, are sayings of the wise.  In either case, these words introduce a short appendix to this part of the book.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:25
segments: Him; the "wicked" man mentioned in

. 
 
  Delight; the pleasant favor of the good.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:27
segments:
Thy work without; thy work which lies out of doors; that is, thy work of agriculture. 
 
  Make it fit for thyself; or, prepare for thyself. 
 
  Afterwards build thy house; a house for elegance and luxury seems to be intended, which should be postponed till other more important work is done. In the warm climate of Palestine a very slight structure serves for the necessary wants of a family.  Another interpretation, Get the materials of thy house ready before thou buildest, is not favored by the original words. 
 
The wise man will postpone works of mere elegance and luxury till he has attended to his more necessary business.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:30
segments: In things spiritual and temporal, the slothful procrastinator may be known by the disordered and decaying condition of what is committed to his care.

entries.title: Proverbs 24:34
segments: One that travelleth; a traveller who comes as an enemy.
